solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Good sieve that's used to make scones

parts.note: a riddle is a coarse sieve used for soil or gravel

explanation.surface: A baker's tip: a good sieve is the tool for scone-making.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests sifting flour, but the sieve is just the word RIDDLE; the scones are cooked on the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat iron plate for cooking on, traditionally used for drop scones and griddle cakes.

clue.text: Fast mover runs and runs around expert

indicators.note: the two run letters are placed either side of the word for expert

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
R again, the cricket abbreviation for runs
an ace is an expert

explanation.surface: An athlete keeps running, lapping a top performer.
explanation.definitionFit: Anything built or trained for speed, such as a car, horse or runner, is called this.

clue.text: Diabolical daughter has come in drunk

indicators.note: drunk means reeling and disordered, so the letters of come in are jumbled

explanation.surface: A parent complains that their wicked daughter has come home inebriated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' rearranges COME IN to EMONIC, which follows D.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something devilish, of or like a demon.

clue.text: Origins of life evidently offering a sign

indicators.note: the origins of words are their opening letters, taken from each of the next three

explanation.surface: Evidence of the beginnings of life presented as a sign.
explanation.definitionFit: Leo is one of the twelve signs of the zodiac, the Lion.

parts.note: as can mean while, as in 'as I was leaving'
set means fixed or rigid, as in set in one's ways

explanation.surface: A valuable thing, and stiff at the same time.
explanation.definitionFit: A useful or valuable possession or quality is called this.

definitions.meaning: charming or pleasing, as in a lovely little cottage
in Britain the dessert course of a meal

explanation.surface: Praise for a lovely dessert.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both pleasant or charming and, in British usage, the dessert course.

clue.text: Old and unexciting — tell me why?

parts.note: ex means former or old, as in ex-wife
plain means ordinary and unexciting

explanation.surface: Someone bored by something dull and dated asks to be told the reason.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a phrase spoken as a request: 'tell me why?' is what one says to ask for this.
explanation.definitionFit: To give reasons or make something clear is exactly what someone asking 'why' wants done.

clue.text: Stray cat pops home to see pile that's rotting

indicators.note: stray suggests wandering about, so the letters of cat pops home wander into a new order

explanation.surface: A wandering cat drops in at home to inspect a rotting heap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stray' looks like an adjective for the cat but signals rearranging CAT POPS HOME.
explanation.definitionFit: A gardener's mound of decaying vegetable matter left to break down into fertiliser.

indicators.note: wild means out of control, so the letters of parties are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A down-and-out who throws riotous parties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tramp' looks like a noun for a vagrant, but it is the verb: to trudge wearily.
explanation.definitionFit: Both verbs mean to walk heavily or wearily over a long way.

definitions.meaning: the chemical element Fe, a common metal
a golf club with an angled metal head

explanation.surface: A club made of metal.
explanation.definitionFit: It is both a metallic element and a type of golf club.

parts.note: to clap is to applaud
a trap is a trick or deception

explanation.surface: Rubbish that involves cheering a trick.
explanation.definitionFit: Pretentious empty talk or rubbish, a synonym.

clue.text: Food like tomatoes brought up for soup

parts.note: chow is slang for food

indicators.note: in a down clue, brought up means the letters are read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: ripe tomatoes are red

explanation.surface: Tomato-based food is served up as soup.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'brought up' reads a word from the bottom, so RED appears as DER; 'like tomatoes' is a colour, not a food.
explanation.definitionFit: A thick soup, typically of clams or fish, such as Manhattan clam chowder with tomatoes.

clue.text: Minor injuries reversed with firm plaster

indicators.note: reversed means the word for minor injuries is read backwards

parts.note: cuts are minor injuries
Co is the abbreviation for company, a firm

explanation.surface: Small wounds treated, and then a firm plaster applied.
explanation.definitionFit: A fine plaster used to coat walls or make decorative mouldings.

indicators.note: furiously suggests wild agitation, so the letters of counter are thrown about

explanation.surface: Pounding a shop counter in a rage.
explanation.definitionFit: To defeat someone heavily is a synonym of beating them soundly.

indicators.note: into means the number is placed inside the word for marijuana

parts.note: pot is slang for marijuana
ten is a number

explanation.surface: Someone claims a quantity of cannabis is powerful stuff.
explanation.definitionFit: Powerful or having great effect, a synonym.

indicators.note: discovered in means found sitting inside the words either mosque

explanation.surface: A flask turned up in one of two mosques.
explanation.definitionFit: A brand of vacuum flask whose name became the general word for one.

definitions.meaning: British slang for a prison sentence, as in doing time
oatmeal cooked in milk or water, eaten in the morning

explanation.surface: An announcement that the morning meal is ready.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Time' in British slang means a jail term, called porridge, after a famous sitcom of that name.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both British slang for a prison term and a hot oat breakfast dish.

clue.text: Commit an offence again? That could be sticky!

parts.note: re- is the prefix meaning again
to sin is to commit an offence

explanation.surface: Reoffending could make things sticky for a criminal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sticky' sounds like an awkward situation but literally describes the gum oozing from trees.
explanation.definitionFit: A gummy substance exuded by trees such as pines is tacky to the touch.

clue.text: Italian island having the skill to make a comeback

indicators.note: a comeback means coming back, so the word for skilled is read backwards

parts.note: able means having the skill to do something

explanation.surface: An island with the ability to return, as Napoleon did from exile there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to make a comeback' turns ABLE round; Napoleon famously came back from exile on this island.
explanation.definitionFit: The island off Tuscany where Napoleon was exiled in 1814.

clue.text: Fundamental principle to inject fish with iodine

indicators.note: to inject means one letter is put inside the word for fish

parts.note: a bass is a fish
I is the chemical symbol for iodine

explanation.surface: A rule of thumb about injecting fish with iodine.
explanation.definitionFit: The underlying foundation of an idea or system, a synonym.

indicators.note: misbehaving means acting out of order, so the letters of roman stud as are disordered

explanation.surface: An unruly Italian ladies' man fancies himself a seer.
explanation.definitionFit: The sixteenth-century French astrologer famed for his cryptic prophecies.

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is said, so the word for morning moisture is heard rather than seen

parts.note: dew is moisture that forms overnight and is seen in the morning

explanation.surface: A weather report says morning damp is on the way.
explanation.definitionFit: Anticipated or scheduled to arrive, as in the train is expected at noon.

indicators.note: entertained by means held inside, so the name sits within the word governess

explanation.surface: A French writer is hosted by a children's governess.
explanation.definitionFit: Jules Verne was the French author of Around the World in Eighty Days.

indicators.note: desperately suggests frantic disorder, so the letters of priests are scrambled

explanation.surface: Clergy desperately keep at their efforts.
explanation.definitionFit: To continue firmly despite difficulty, a synonym of persevering.
